distractors.reason: We don't say 'big advertising' to describe ads aimed at specific people. 'Big' describes size, not the purpose of the campaign.
We don't say 'strong advertising' for ads aimed at specific groups. 'Strong' suits feelings, drinks or arguments, not this kind of advertising.
We don't say 'fast advertising' for ads aimed at specific people. 'Fast' describes speed, which is not the point of the collocation.

example_sentence: Many companies use ___ advertising to reach specific customers.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku mogą przetłumaczyć 'duża' dosłownie jako 'big' i powiedzieć 'big advertising' zamiast poprawnego 'targeted advertising'.
explanation: In English, 'targeted' describes advertising aimed at a specific group of people, based on their interests, age or behaviour. The adjective shows the purpose of the campaign, not its size.

related_collocations.example: Online advertising has grown quickly in the last ten years.
The regulator fined the company for misleading advertising.
The campaign used viral marketing to spread the video quickly.

memory_tip: TARGETED = aimed at a specific group (targeted ads, targeted campaigns) | BIG = size (big screen, big budget)
